scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: Hello, one of our IT lab machines (the one called
it_lab3) has dropped off the network completely -- from that machine you
can't reach anything at all, not even the first thing it's supposed to talk
to. The other machines around it are fine, it's just that one. The student
who uses it swears they didn't change anything, and someone here wondered if
"its port died", whatever that means. Could someone take a look at why just
that one machine is cut off? Thanks a lot!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
No network fault exists. The helpdesk ticket claims that it_lab3 "can't reach
anything, not even the first hop," but every diagnostic probe contradicts this.
The machine has a properly configured eth0 interface (192.168.1.5/24, state
UP/LOWER_UP, link detected, no errors or drops). Its default gateway
(router0 at 192.168.1.1) is reachable with 0% packet loss. All same-LAN
peers (it_hod, it_lab1, it_lab2) respond normally. Remote segments are equally
accessible: cs_hod on lan_cs, pc0 on lan_principle, pc1 on lan_servers, and
pc2 on lan_internet all return 0% loss pings from it_lab3. Inbound
reachability is also confirmed — it_lab1 pings it_lab3 without issue. The
switch0 bridge (br0) that connects lan_it to router0 has both ports UP with
zero errors. The routing table on it_lab3 (connected subnet + default via
192.168.1.1) is identical to the other working IT lab hosts. There is no
misconfiguration, no interface failure, and no switching or routing anomaly
anywhere in the path. The reported symptom does not reflect the current
network state; this is a false-premise ticket. No corrective action is
required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes it_lab3 holds its address and reaches its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states it_lab3 retains 192.168.1.5/24 and that the default gateway 192.168.1.1 is reachable with 0% packet loss.

The agent's conclusions are directly supported by the recorded commands and their outputs: interface state, IP and route, successful same-LAN and off-segment pings (including gateway), and inbound reachability were all observed. The investigation covers the essential checks and the inferences follow logically from the evidence.
